question: Use this fictional ABI with decimal byte addresses. A D object begins at 1000; its L base is at offset 0 and R base at offset 16. The R-view virtual table has an f entry implemented by an adjustor thunk that subtracts 16 from the incoming R pointer before invoking D::f. A different entry invokes non-overridden R::g without adjustment. Calling both through the R pointer 1016, what is the pair (this address inside D::f, this address inside R::g)? No real-machine layout is implied.
explanation: The f thunk converts the R-subobject pointer back to the most-derived D address: 1016-16=1000. R::g expects its own R subobject and receives 1016 unchanged. Multiple-inheritance dispatch can require this-adjustment rather than only selecting a function address.
